title: [Group Project] - Sprite Editor
summary: Pixel art sprite editor with frame timeline, bucket fill, and animation support

data.text: A 32×32 pixel art sprite editor with frame-based animation, built as a group project for CS 3505 (Software Practice II) at the University of Utah with 6 contributors. I authored 54 of 116 commits (~47%) and was the primary developer for the drawing engine, frame management system, and application architecture — contributing roughly 55–65% of the final source code across the model and view layers.

items.content: Built the entire pixel editing canvas — a 640×640 widget rendering a 32×32 sprite at 20× zoom with coordinate mapping between screen pixels and sprite pixels

Implemented mouse event handling for hover highlighting, click-to-paint, and drag-to-draw with a layered paintEvent pipeline: checkerboard transparency background → frame image → painted pixels → hover highlight → grid overlay
Implemented bucket fill using a DFS (depth-first search) flood-fill algorithm with a stack-based traversal of neighboring pixels matching the target color
Added variable brush size (1px to 32px) with area-based painting that iterates over a square brush footprint, wired to a UI slider
Wired the eraser tool to paint with Qt::transparent on the canvas, integrating it with the toolbar's tool selection system
Designed the Frame data model managing an ordered std::vector of QImage frames with add, remove, copy, swap (reorder), clear, and select operations
Built the FramesView timeline panel (100% sole author) — a vertical list of 128×128 clickable thumbnails with yellow highlight on the selected frame and dynamic height calculation
Implemented insert-after-selected frame positioning, deep-copy frame, and swap frames for reordering — with edge case handling (last frame clears instead of deleting)
Added scroll auto-focus that automatically scrolls the timeline to the newest frame when one is added

Established the Model-View architecture and signal/slot wiring pattern used by all team members — created the initial project structure, model file, and the setModel() pattern for connecting views to the centralized SpriteEditorModel
Made a key architectural decision to migrate pixel storage from a raw 2D array to QImage, enabling native Qt rendering and simplifying the save/load pipeline
Built the core SpriteEditorModel — the central state manager owning the Frame instance, coordinating signals between views, and providing the drawing API (updateFrame, bucketAlgorithm)
Connected the color palette to the edit canvas, fixed color selection not updating on the drawing pane
Fixed bugs: eraser leaving extra pixels, unwanted initial pixel when adding new frames, bucket tool misbehavior after switching from eraser
Wrote documentation across header files (editview.h, framesview.h, mainview.h, model.h, previewpaneview.h), created the Code Style Document and README
Restructured editview.cpp for cleaner code organization and adjusted overall UI layout and widget positioning
Languages: C++
Frameworks: Qt 6, QWidget, QImage, QPainter, QTimer, QColorDialog, QScrollArea
Patterns: Model-View separation, Observer pattern (Qt signals/slots), centralized wiring hub (MainWindow)
Algorithms: DFS flood fill (bucket tool), coordinate mapping with zoom factor, area-based brush painting

Concepts: Pixel-level rendering with layered compositing (checkerboard → image → overlay → grid), mouse event handling (press/move/release/leave), frame-based animation, QImage as a mutable pixel buffer
Tools: Git (collaborative branching, 54 commits), QMake, GitHub
